message:
Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the clamped frame for the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) holds with large margin because the demand is car-scale against High Strength Friction Grip (HSFG, preloaded high-strength bolts) slip capacity in the HSFG bolts guidance (E30). The demand is the factored frame design load (E36) of 12.3 kN, about one small car, carried on two transverse bearers in the bolted frame sketch (E37), so slip does not govern.

Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the moving mass stays clear under crowd load because the stroke is thumbnail-scale against the stop clearance in the same sketch. The deciding dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) is 20.1 mm, giving 2.49 times margin to plus-minus 50.0 mm stops, after the static weight of 4.90 kN from the TMD weight calculation (E35), about seven body weights, is already carried on the springs.

Elena, Marcus, Tomas, the retrofit stays hidden and serviceable while meeting comfort because all change is below deck with removable cover plus shims for re-tuning in the staged access concept (C4). The residual dense-crowd acceleration scaling (E52) is 0.545 m/s2, equal to 0.0556 times gravity like gentle bus braking, below the 1.00 m/s2 minimum-comfort bound. Ready, because load, clearance and access now close jointly.
